summary: How often numbers are checked, such as every month, every season or every year.
example: Monthly Cycle: the numbers on it are checked once a month.
definition: How often numbers are reported, and when each report is due. A cycle is either equal periods, such as every three months from September, or named periods, such as terms or survey rounds, each named by the month it ends. It also says how many days after a period ends the report is due. Each KPI names one cycle. It is not how often a data source changes, not the time span of a goal, and not a single report.

/spec/periodMonths.guide: How many months each period lasts: 1, 3, 6 or 12. Choose one your data sources can keep up with.

poor.text: 1, for measures read from forms transcribed once a season
poor.why: The source only has new numbers once a season, so most months would have nothing to report.

/spec/startMonth.guide: The month the first period starts, from 1 to 12. This sets which month each period ends in.
good: 9, for a cooperative whose season year opens in September

poor.text: 1, for a seasonal cycle when the season year opens in September
poor.why: Periods would end in March, June, September and December, cutting across the seasons the readings describe.

/spec/periods.guide: Named periods, for when equal months do not fit, such as terms or survey rounds. Give each a name and the month it ends: a month of the year if it repeats, or a year and month if it happens once.
good: Term I ends in month 12, Term II in 4, Term III in 7

poor.text: Quarterly, for readings taken at the end of each term
poor.why: Quarters end in March, June, September and December, which are not when terms end. Name the terms instead.
With no periods, a missed reading cannot show. Name the waves by the month each ends.

/spec/periods/-/name.guide: The period's name. Each name must be different.

/spec/periods/-/endMonth.guide: For a period that repeats each year: the month it ends, 1 to 12. The year starts the month after the last period ends.

/spec/periods/-/end.guide: For a period that happens once: the year and month it ends.

/spec/dueOffsetDays.guide: How many days after a period ends the report is due.
good: 14, for a seasonal cycle whose forms are transcribed in the two weeks after the season

poor.text: 0, when the figures take weeks to transcribe
poor.why: Every round would be late on the day it closes.

/metadata/name.guide: The cycle's name, such as Monthly.

KPI:/spec/cycle.ask: Which KPIs are read on this cycle?
KPI:/spec/cycle.ifNone: None yet is fine. A KPI names this cycle when you set how it is measured.
